speaker: Doctor
text: Let's start by asking about your symptoms. Have you been experiencing headaches, dizziness, or vision changes recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 5-year-old boy. The patient is presented by his mother for a well-child visit. The boy was born at 39 weeks gestation via spontaneous vaginal delivery, is currently up to date on all vaccines, and is meeting all developmental milestones. His mother reports that he has been generally doing well with no concerns. No family history of cardiovascular disease. The boy does not take any medications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the blood pressure was found to be elevated during this well-child visit, have you noticed any swelling in his ankles or hands, or any changes in his urine output? REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis and Basic Metabolic Panel.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is High blood pressure on the right upper extremity. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Migraine and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: There seems to be a misunderstanding; a 5-year-old cannot have a migraine as the primary cause of unilateral high blood pressure. Can you confirm if you are the child, or is there another child in the family who is experiencing these symptoms? If the child is asymptomatic, I need to examine his feet to check for lower extremity blood pressure measurements and look for signs of a renal abnormality or coarctation.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Born full term with an uneventful neonatal period. Social history: Patient attends kindergarten. Lives with parents and one younger sibling. No exposure to tobacco smoke.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Coarctation of the Aorta.

Please confirm the blood pressure in the lower extremities (legs) immediately; a significantly lower reading in the legs compared to the arms is diagnostic.
